analysis.note: Relative pronoun; printed with visarga loss before the following vowel in ya enaṃ.
Accusative object; Śaṅkara glosses the referent as prakṛtaṃ dehinam, ‘the embodied one under discussion.’
Agent-noun in the accusative: ‘as the slayer/agent of killing.’
Second relative pronoun, correlative with tau ubhau.
Printed together with the following pronoun as cainaṃ = ca + enam.
Second occurrence of the same accusative pronoun; printed in vowel sandhi with ca.
Ātmanepada form used in kartari sense: ‘thinks/considers.’
Kta participial stem from √han, agreeing with enam; Śaṅkara takes it as the object/patient of the act of killing.
Correlative pronoun picking up the two yaḥ-clauses.
Third dual present: ‘the two do not understand/know’; final visarga appears as -o before na in the printed sandhi.
Printed together with the following pronoun as nāyaṃ = na + ayam.
Nominative subject of hanti and hanyate; Śaṅkara glosses it as ayam ātmā.
Kartari present: ‘kills’; denied of the Self.
Passive present: ‘is killed’; Śaṅkara denies patienthood/object-status in killing of the Self.

justifications.decision: The pronouns enam and ayam refer to the dehin/ātman, not to the physical body as such.
options_considered: ‘this body’ as the thing that kills or is killed
‘this person’ in a merely ordinary sense
‘this embodied self / Self’ as the topic under discussion

evidence.quote: ya enaṃ prakṛtaṃ dehinaṃ vetti vijānāti
evidence.translation: ‘He who knows this—the embodied one under discussion—understands...’

justifications.decision: hantāram is to be understood technically as the agent of the act of killing, not merely as a loose epithet ‘murderer.’
options_considered: the kartṛ, agent, in hanana-kriyā, the act of killing
justifications.chosen: ‘as the slayer,’ i.e. as agent of the act of killing

evidence.translation: ‘hantāram: the agent of the act of killing.’

evidence.quote: na ayam atmā hanti na hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartā bhavati
evidence.translation: ‘This Self does not kill; it does not become the agent of the act of killing.’

justifications.decision: hatam and hanyate mark the Self as imagined patient/object of killing; Śaṅkara rejects that patienthood, especially as arising from identification with killing of the body.
options_considered: hatam simply as ‘dead’ in a physical sense
hatam as ‘slain,’ the karma/patient of the act of killing, wrongly projected onto the Self through body-killing
justifications.chosen: ‘slain,’ with the sense ‘made the object/patient of killing’ only in the mistaken view

evidence.quote: manyate hataṃ deha-hananena hato 'ham iti hanana-kriyāyāḥ karma-bhūtam
evidence.translation: ‘[He] thinks [this] slain: “I am slain by the killing of the body,” as having become the object of the act of killing.’

evidence.quote: na ca hanyate na ca karma bhavatīty arthaḥ
evidence.translation: ‘Nor is it killed; that means, it does not become the object [of the action].’

justifications.decision: ubhau tau na vijānītaḥ means that the two mistaken cognizers do not truly know the Self; ubhau tau are the dual subject, not an object.
options_considered: ‘both of them do not know [the Self]’
justifications.chosen: ‘both of them do not know,’ namely they do not know the Self’s true nature

evidence.quote: tau ubhau na vijānītaḥ na jñātavantau avivekena ātmānam
evidence.translation: ‘Those two both do not know; through non-discrimination they have not known the Self.’

evidence.quote: yau vijānītaḥ tau ātma-svarūpānabhijñau ity arthaḥ
evidence.translation: ‘Those two who understand [in that way] are ignorant of the Self’s own nature—this is the meaning.’

justifications.decision: The final pāda is a metaphysical denial of agency and patienthood in the changeless Self, not an ethical injunction or a denial that bodily killing occurs.
options_considered: ‘do not kill, and do not be killed’ as injunction
‘this body does not kill and is not killed’
‘this Self neither acts as killer nor undergoes being killed, because it is changeless’
justifications.chosen: ‘This Self neither kills nor is killed,’ grounded in avikriyatva, changelessness

evidence.quote: na ca karma bhavatīty arthaḥ, avikriyatvāt
evidence.translation: ‘Nor does it become the object [of the act]; this is the meaning, because it is changeless.’

justifications.decision: The two yaḥ-clauses are correlative with tau ubhau and identify two mistaken standpoints, the second explicitly ‘another’ according to the commentary.
options_considered: one and the same person described twice
two persons/standpoints: one who thinks the Self kills, another who thinks it is killed
justifications.chosen: two mistaken cognizers: ‘whoever knows it as slayer, and whoever thinks it slain—both...’

evidence.quote: ya ca enam anyo manyate hataṃ
evidence.translation: ‘And another who thinks this one slain...’

translation:
Whoever knows this embodied Self as the slayer,
and whoever thinks this one slain—
both of them do not know.
This Self does not kill, nor is it killed.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind rendering might take enam as the body or an ordinary person; Śaṅkara identifies it as the dehin/ātman under discussion.
It might translate hantāram and hatam merely as ‘killer’ and ‘dead,’ missing Śaṅkara’s kartṛ/karma analysis of agency and patienthood in the act of killing.
It might read the final statement ethically or physically, whereas the bhāṣya makes it a claim about the changeless Self’s non-agency and non-patienthood.
It might leave na vijānītaḥ without its supplied object; Śaṅkara states that the two fail to know the Self due to non-discrimination.
mula: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaś cainaṃ manyate hatam | ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
commentary_lines: ya enaṃ prakṛtaṃ dehinaṃ vetti vijānāti hantāraṃ hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartāraṃ ya ca enam anyo manyate hataṃ deha-hananena hato 'ham iti hanana-kriyāyāḥ karma-bhūtam |
tau ubhau na vijānītaḥ na jñātavantau avivekena ātmānam |
hantā ahaṃ, hato 'smy aham iti deha-hananena ātmānam ahaṃ pratyaya-viṣayaṃ yau vijānītaḥ tau ātma-svarūpānabhijñau ity arthaḥ |
yasmāt na ayam atmā hanti na hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartā bhavati, na ca hanyate na ca karma bhavatīty arthaḥ, avikriyatvāt ||bhgs_2.19||
